United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative: During the 42 C/5 implementation, the Natural Sciences, Communication and Information, and Culture programmes collaborated to integrate UNESCO's capacities in Indigenous knowledge systems, cultural practices, heritage, and the role of information technologies in promoting Indigenous languages. The Strategy for 43 C/5 builds upon this foundation, supported by all three programmes, focusing on fostering innovation in practice and policy. In this context, the Science Sector contributes by integrating Indigenous knowledge into global sustainability frameworks, ensuring that traditional ecological wisdom informs climate adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and policy development. On the other hand, the Communication and Information programme leverages initiatives such as the International Decade of Indigenous Languages to promote linguistic diversity online, develop language technologies, and document Indigenous knowledge systems to prevent their erosion. There is growing recognition of the importance of Indigenous heritage for sustainable development, cultural diversity, and resilience, many Indigenous languages and knowledge systems remain at risk due to marginalization, insufficient documentation, and the impacts of globalization.
